summary: @workoscalif/sudoku ships opaque x64 Go binary executed at postinstall under a C-source cover story
details: The package declares itself as a sudoku generator with a small C source at native/gridgen.c (~250 lines) and a postinstall script that spawns vendor/gridgen-<platform>-<arch> with three positional arguments. The shipped x64 binaries do not match that story: vendor/gridgen-darwin-x64 and vendor/gridgen-linux-x64 are byte-identical (sha256 05b69666193e8fa719c37df22833bf36a120b15e2408a9ecd47e34f140a44420, 33,648,788 bytes), both are ELF (so the file named darwin-x64 is not a Mach-O), and both contain Go runtime markers (runtime., GODEBUG=, chacha8, /proc/self/cgroup) that cannot be produced by compiling the shipped C source. The arm64 binaries are the small C-compiled artifacts consistent with native/gridgen.c, so only the x64 variants diverge. The postinstall hook runs spawnSync on this binary at install time and swallows all errors, exiting 0 regardless of what the binary does. Installing the package on a linux-x64 or darwin-x64 host executes opaque, publisher-controlled code that mismatches the declared native source.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
